item.title: Team Fiji defend Restaurant Challenge title, crowned overall champions in Australia
item.description: Team Fiji has successfully defended its Restaurant Challenge title in Australia, emerging as the overall winners while bringing home gold, silver and bronze medals across several culinary competitions. Chef Isireli Chong of Club Wyndham Resort and Chef Filipe of Yasawa Island Resort led Fiji’s success, winning gold in the Restaurant Challenge.
item.content:encoded:
Team Fiji has successfully defended its Restaurant Challenge title in Australia, emerging as the overall winners while bringing home gold, silver and bronze medals across several culinary competitions.

Chef Isireli Chong of Club Wyndham Resort and Chef Filipe of Yasawa Island Resort led Fiji’s success, winning gold in the Restaurant Challenge.

Their performance helped Team Fiji successfully defend the title and be crowned the overall winners of the competition.

Chef Ifraaz Hussein and Chef Frances Wakeham of Sheraton Fiji Golf & Beach Resort also delivered a strong performance, finishing second and securing a silver medal in the Restaurant Challenge.

Fiji also picked up medals in the individual cook-off, with Chef Maurisio and Chef Masi of COMO Laucala Island both securing bronze medals.

Meanwhile, Chef Warren Mave added another international medal for Fiji after winning bronze at the Global Pastry Chefs Challenge Pacific Rim Semi-Finals in Melbourne.

The results mean Fiji finishes its Australian campaign with gold and the overall Restaurant Challenge title, silver in the Restaurant Challenge, bronze medals in the individual cook-off and another bronze from the Global Pastry Chefs Challenge Pacific Rim Semi-Finals.

The achievements highlight the depth of talent within Fiji's culinary industry, with the chefs demonstrating their skills, teamwork and professionalism on the international stage.

Team Fiji says the success is also an inspiration for young chefs around the country who hope to one day represent Fiji internationally.

item.description: From studying under a kerosene lamp in Levuka to becoming Fiji’s first in-country trained gynaecological oncologist, Dr Nanise Sikiti’s journey is one of sacrifice, resilience and determination. item.content:encoded:
From studying under a kerosene lamp in Levuka to becoming Fiji’s first in-country trained gynaecological oncologist, Dr Nanise Sikiti’s journey is one of sacrifice, resilience and determination.

Dr Sikiti will share her inspiring story on fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono on Wednesday at 7pm.

Dr Sikiti will share the beginning of her journey in humble surroundings in Levuka.

She will also speak about the sacrifices she has made throughout her career, the challenges of balancing family and professional responsibilities, and the people and experiences that have shaped the woman and doctor she is today.

item.title: Radrodro hits back at Kumar over Education Ministry issues
item.description: Minister for Education Aseri Radrodro has hit back at Opposition MP and former Education Minister Premila Kumar, saying she should be the last person to speak on issues concerning the Ministry of Education. In response to Kumar's comments that Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka should consider replacing Radrodro if he cannot resolve what she describes as recurring salary and allowance issues affecting
item.content:encoded:
Minister for Education Aseri Radrodro has hit back at Opposition MP and former Education Minister Premila Kumar, saying she should be the last person to speak on issues concerning the Ministry of Education.

In response to Kumar's comments that Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka should consider replacing Radrodro if he cannot resolve what she describes as recurring salary and allowance issues affecting teachers, Radrodro claims the Ministry is still trying to address issues left behind by Kumar and her former Director of Human Resources.

He says some officers were appointed during their tenure, and the Ministry now has to work with them and teach them how to operate professionally and do things correctly.

Radrodro also says he is still dealing with cases involving teachers who have remained unpaid for several years, including during Kumar's tenure as Education Minister.

He says the difference under the Coalition Government is that teachers are now allowed to speak up about their grievances, either through their teacher unions or by communicating directly with his office.

He claims that during Kumar's tenure, teachers were scared to publicly voice their complaints and the two teacher unions were ignored.

Radrodro says his office does its best to address concerns raised by teachers.

On the current pay issues affecting teachers, Radrodro says he has instructed the Permanent Secretary for Education to seek assistance from the Permanent Secretary for Finance to have the affected teachers' payments processed immediately.

item.title: Kumar calls for Radrodro to be replaced if he cannot resolve teachers’ pay issues
item.description: Opposition MP Premila Kumar says Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka should consider replacing Education Minister Aseri Radrodro if he cannot resolve what she describes as recurring salary and allowance issues affecting teachers and their pay. Kumar says teachers should not have to chase the Government for money they have already earned and should not be punished for administrative failures within the
item.content:encoded:
Opposition MP Premila Kumar says Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka should consider replacing Education Minister Aseri Radrodro if he cannot resolve what she describes as recurring salary and allowance issues affecting teachers and their pay.

Kumar says teachers should not have to chase the Government for money they have already earned and should not be punished for administrative failures within the Ministry of Education.

She says teachers were paid only up to Pay 18, with payments subsequently stopped after a Ministry audit reportedly found that some signed contracts had not been returned.

Kumar has questioned where the systems and people responsible for ensuring these contracts are properly processed are.

She says there are Heads of Schools and Divisional Heads in all four divisions, and if administrative problems are occurring on this scale, they should have been identified and resolved earlier.

Kumar claims that teachers who graduated in 2024 and submitted applications for salary upgrades, along with their degrees and university letters confirming completion of their studies, are still waiting for payment.

She says Education Minister Aseri Radrodro had confirmed that 273 teachers would be paid, subject to the availability of funds.

The Opposition MP also raised concerns about teachers taking additional classes because of teacher shortages and those serving in acting positions who she says are still waiting for allowances and other payments.

Kumar says the latest situation follows previous reports of salary and allowance problems affecting teachers.

She says Radrodro announced last month that salary arrears for 318 Ministry of Education staff were being expedited through Pay 17 and Pay 18, with the Ministry saying the delays were associated with internal processing and compliance requirements.

Ku mar says the Fijian Teachers Association has also publicly raised concerns about salary and allowance delays affecting teachers .

She says while teachers must comply with the Civil Service Code of Conduct and follow proper administrative channels, questions need to be asked about what happens when those channels do not work.

Kumar has also questioned what teachers are expected to do when their grievances are repeatedly raised but remain unresolved by the Ministry.

She says they understand some teachers have even written to the Prime Minister’s Office seeking assistance.

K umar has also questioned the role of Minister for Employment Agni Deo Singh, saying workers’ rights cannot be selective and teachers employed by the Government should not be ignored.

She says teachers should not be portrayed as irresponsible for allegedly failing to submit documents, sign contracts or follow procedures if they have already provided the required documentation and it has not been processed by the Ministry.

Kumar says if teachers have submitted all the required documentation and the paperwork is sitting somewhere within the Ministry, they should not be punished for the Ministry’s failure to process it.

We have sent questions to the Ministry of Education seeking a response to Kumar’s concerns.

item.title: Kiran calls for stronger mental health support for servicewomen
item.description: Minister for Women, Children and Social Protection Sashi Kiran has warned that Fiji cannot expect its servicewomen to protect others if they are not provided with the psychological support needed to protect themselves and their loved ones. Kiran made the comments at the closing of a five-day Republic of Fiji Military Forces Servicewomen Mental Health and Wellbeing Workshop held at Pasifika Communi
item.content:encoded:
Minister for Women, Children and Social Protection Sashi Kiran has warned that Fiji cannot expect its servicewomen to protect others if they are not provided with the psychological support needed to protect themselves and their loved ones.

Kiran made the comments at the closing of a five-day Republic of Fiji Military Forces Servicewomen Mental Health and Wellbeing Workshop held at Pasifika Communities University.

The workshop, held under the theme “Breaking the Cycles,” provided servicewomen with a safe space to discuss trauma, mental health and healing, while building confidence to recognise distress and seek support.

Kiran says servicewomen operate in demanding environments while also carrying responsibilities within their families and communities.

She says exposure to conflict, danger and the suffering of others can leave deep and unseen wounds that may affect personnel, their families and relationships after returning home.

Kiran also stressed that mental health and wellbeing are essential to operational readiness, discipline, leadership and sustained performance.

She acknowledged the contribution of Fiji’s servicewomen to United Nations peacekeeping missions, humanitarian operations and disaster response, saying their professionalism and courage had earned Fiji international respect.

The Minister also highlighted challenges servicewomen may face, including family pressures, harassment, workplace discrimination, domestic violence and climate-related emergencies.

She encouraged the servicewomen to continue supporting one another and promoting an environment where personnel feel respected and safe to seek help.

She thanked the Australian Government, through the Fiji Program Support Platform, and the RFMF Psychology Cell for supporting the workshop.

Second Lieutenant Loata Lolomatanoa says the five-day programme was a meaningful journey of learning, reflection and personal growth.

She says participants felt safe to speak, listen and reflect on issues that were not always easy to discuss.

item.title: Men and fathers urged to rethink traditional gender roles to address violence - Dr Cliff
item.description: Men and fathers across the Pacific are being urged to rethink how they raise their sons and challenge traditional gender roles in the home as part of efforts to address gender-based violence. While speaking at the Pacific Islands Health Research Symposium, UnitingWorld Pacific Office Regional Coordinator Rev. Dr Cliff Bird says while there are many positive cultural practices in the way Pacific fa
item.content:encoded:
Men and fathers across the Pacific are being urged to rethink how they raise their sons and challenge traditional gender roles in the home as part of efforts to address gender-based violence.

While speaking at the Pacific Islands Health Research Symposium, UnitingWorld Pacific Office Regional Coordinator Rev. Dr Cliff Bird says while there are many positive cultural practices in the way Pacific families socialise and raise their children that should be maintained, there are also practices that need to be reconsidered, particularly those relating to gender roles and relationships.

Rev. Dr Bird says through his work with churches and communities across the Pacific, he has encountered cases where violence was perpetrated against women and girls because they did not fulfil household chores expected of them based on traditional gender roles.

Insert:Rev. Dr Bird on Fathers 5th Sept 26

He also highlights the high prevalence of gender-based violence across Pacific countries and says violence is also occurring within churches and faith-based communities.

Rev. Dr Bird says there also needs to be critical rethinking of how the Bible and other holy scriptures are read and interpreted, particularly passages that have historically been used to justify the dominance of men and the domestication or silencing of women and girls.

He says religious teachings should instead affirm and empower women and girls, children and other vulnerable people.

He acknowledges work already being undertaken by churches and faith-based organisations in Fiji, including the House of Sarah, the Methodist Church in Fiji's Family Life Ministry and the Catholic Church's Women at the Well Ministry, but says these initiatives need to be strengthened and resourced.

Rev. Dr Bird also highlights Gender Equality Theology, which he and his wife started in the region with Pacific partner churches and United Churches in Australia, saying theological and biblical resources developed through the initiative are being used by churches and faith-based organisations across the Pacific.

He says men can play a greater role in addressing gender-based violence through men's fellowship groups, male advocacy programmes, male champions, role models and initiatives such as the House of Sarah's men as change agents.

Rev. Dr Bird says existing men's groups and networks have the potential to address gender-based violence more intentionally in their activities with men and boys.

He also identifies sport as another important area where gender-based violence needs to be addressed, saying sporting facilities should be safe spaces for everyone.

He says work is already being undertaken in Fiji and Samoa through rugby and increasingly across some Pacific islands through football, but communities need to consider frameworks that mainstream dignity, safety, health and equality in sport.

Rev. Dr Bird also highlights Project Goalkeeper in the Solomon Islands, which links faith and sport in addressing gender-based violence.

The initiative was developed with the Solomon Islands Football Federation, Solomon Islands National Sports Council, UN Women and member churches of the Solomon Islands Christian Association.

He says the resource provides Bible studies and other educational and advocacy material for use at village and community level, with the Solomon Islands Football Federation preparing to roll it out in identified rural communities.

Rev. Dr Bird says men and boys have the opportunity to become agents of change in addressing gender-based violence, not only in homes and churches but also in communities and sport.

item.title: Adi Salamalawa's parents say strong families key to protecting young people from drugs
item.description: As Miss Hibiscus 2026 Adi Salamalawa Korosaya celebrates her victory with her family on Father’s Day, her parents are urging parents to lead by example and spend more time with their children, saying strong family values and guidance at home are key to protecting young people from challenges faced by youths such as drugs. The 23-year-old spent her first day as Miss Hibiscus with her parents and fa
item.content:encoded:
As Miss Hibiscus 2026 Adi Salamalawa Korosaya celebrates her victory with her family on Father’s Day, her parents are urging parents to lead by example and spend more time with their children, saying strong family values and guidance at home are key to protecting young people from challenges faced by youths such as drugs.

The 23-year-old spent her first day as Miss Hibiscus with her parents and family at Centenary Church, where she gave thanks to God following her victory last night.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Adi Sala says making her parents happy is what makes her happy.

Insert: Adi Salamalawa on making parents happy 6th Sept 26

Her father, Matai Korosaya, says the victory is a special Father’s Day gift and thanked God for giving the family the strength, courage and support throughout the journey.

Insert: Matai - Tavua this is for you Sept 06

Matai, who has four children, says he is grateful that the 70th Hibiscus Festival has placed emphasis on young people and families.

He says the message was also reflected in the sermon at Centenary Church today, which focused on helping and protecting children from challenges affecting the country, including drugs.

Matai says when people ask why so many young people are facing difficulties, the answer comes back to family.

He says the key is the family, and parents have to understand that children watch their behaviour and often follow what they see at home.

Matai says he is not someone who likes to preach, stressing that actions speak louder than words.

He says parents need to set a good example for their children and make time for them, adding that spending quality time with his children has always been important to him.

Adi Salamalawa 's mother, Sereima Bokini-Korosaya, says Centenary Church has played an important role in nurturing her daughter's spiritual life and shaping her into the young woman she is today.

She says Adi Salamalawa and her siblings were brought to church from a young age and attended Sunday school, while both parents remained involved in their spiritual upbringing as they grew older.

Se reima is encouraging fathers and other parents to continue supporting their children, spend more time with them at home, teach them strong values and keep them grounded in their Christian faith.

She says young people have the potential and ability to achieve their goals, but this requires hard work, determination, courage and a strong support system from their families.

Sereima believes children are carrying some of the heaviest burdens from the social issues affecting communities and says the solution to many of these challenges begins at home.

Meanwhile, celebrations are expected to continue for the Korosaya family, with Matai saying the victory has brought joy to Daliconi and their wider traditional communities.

item.title: Fatherhood is an honour and a responsibility - PM
item.description: Fatherhood is an honour and a responsibility. This is a message shared by Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka as Fiji celebrates Father’s Day today, highlighting the responsibility of fathers to protect, provide, guide and set an example for their children.
item.content:encoded:
Fatherhood is an honour and a responsibility.

This is a message shared by Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka as Fiji celebrates Father’s Day today, highlighting the responsibility of fathers to protect, provide, guide and set an example for their children.

He acknowledges that fathers will make mistakes but says one of the greatest lessons they can give their children is showing them how to acknowledge their mistakes, make amends and get back up again.

Rabuka says fathers play an important role in shaping the future of Fiji, with the values demonstrated in homes today reflected in the country children build tomorrow.
